title: RS_TileExplode
description: >
  Splits a raster into a grid of fixed-size tiles, returning one list item per
  tile with its grid position.
kernels:
  - returns: list
    args:
    - raster
    - {name: tile_width, type: integer}
    - {name: tile_height, type: integer}
  - returns: list
    args:
    - raster
    - name: tile_width
      type: integer
      description: Tile width in pixels. Must be >= 1.
    - name: tile_height
      type: integer
      description: Tile height in pixels. Must be >= 1.
    - name: options
      type: string
      description: >
        JSON options object. `bands`: a list of 1-based band indices to include
        in each tile, in order (default: all bands). `pad_with_nodata`: when
        true, pad the last partial row/column of tiles to the full tile size
        with a nodata fill (default: false). `nodata`: the value written to
        padded pixels (only valid with `pad_with_nodata = true`); defaults to
        the band's own nodata value, or the band data type's minimum if it has
        none. It is an error if `nodata` does not fit the band's data type.
---

::: callout-warning
**Experimental.** This function is experimental; its behavior may change without notice.
:::

## Description

`RS_TileExplode` cuts a raster into a grid of `tile_width` x `tile_height`
tiles, returning a list with one item per tile. It mirrors Sedona Spark's
`RS_TileExplode`; because SedonaDB has no per-row generator, the tiles are
returned as a list that you `UNNEST` to get one row per tile.

Each returned list item is a struct with:

- `x`: the tile's grid column (0-based), counting from the left
- `y`: the tile's grid row (0-based), counting from the top
- `tile`: the tile raster, with a geotransform shifted to the tile's own origin

The grid is `ceil(width / tile_width)` columns by `ceil(height / tile_height)`
rows. When the raster does not divide evenly, the last column and row of tiles
are partial: by default the smaller edge tile is emitted as-is, but with
`pad_with_nodata = true` those tiles are padded to the full tile size with a
nodata fill.

## Examples

```sql
SELECT RS_TileExplode(RS_Example(), 32, 16);
```

Selecting only the first band and padding the edge tiles:

```sql
SELECT RS_TileExplode(
  RS_Example(),
  40,
  20,
  '{"bands": [1], "pad_with_nodata": true, "nodata": 0}'
);
```
